note: 150 Moments of Questionable Serenity: recovery humor. The recoverymisfits house account posts one every other day at noon Eastern, in this order, then starts over (supabase/functions/porch-daily). Edit a line and push to change one; add new ones at the END so the order that already ran stays put.
items: I asked God to remove my shortcomings. Apparently there's a waiting list.
I'm learning to sit with my feelings. Neither of us is happy about the seating arrangement.
My higher power has excellent timing. I have filed several complaints.
Today I practiced acceptance. Tomorrow I may attempt it without the heavy sigh.
I paused when agitated. Unfortunately, my face continued the conversation.
I'm staying in today. My anxiety has already booked next Thursday.
I no longer need to be right about everything. Just the things currently being discussed.
Asked for a sign. Got a suggestion. Typical.
I surrendered this morning. By lunch I had requested several amendments.
My resentment list has subfolders.
I went to a meeting for answers. They gave me a folding chair and something to think about.
I'm working on humility. I'd tell you how well it's going, but apparently that's part of the problem.
My sponsor asked what my part was. I was hoping we could focus on the cast members I dislike.
I can accept people exactly as they are. Once they make these three minor adjustments.
I turned it over. Then checked to see how it was being handled.
My first sober hobby was explaining why every suggestion wouldn't work for me.
I finally found inner peace. Someone immediately asked me where we keep the scissors.
I'm listening without interrupting. The rebuttal is still being prepared, but quietly.
I don't hold grudges. I maintain a small historical archive.
I'm taking life one day at a time. Some days come with an unreasonable number of hours.
My sponsor said to keep it simple. I asked for clarification in four paragraphs.
I'm becoming more open-minded. Please submit your ideas in the format I prefer.
I came to recovery willing to do anything. There were a few exclusions in the fine print.
Today I chose peace. I would still like everyone to know I was right.
My higher power doesn't need my help. This has been difficult news for management.
I used to think a spiritual awakening would involve a bright light. So far it's involved returning a phone call.
I'm not judging. I'm having a very detailed private reaction.
I said the Serenity Prayer. The person driving in front of me has not read it.
I'm learning to ask for help before a crisis. Currently I ask during the opening credits.
The meeting topic was patience. Naturally, the person before me shared for eleven minutes.
I made a gratitude list. Then remembered something annoying and gave it equal billing.
I want a quiet mind. Mine would like to make one final announcement.
I thought I was sharing my experience. Apparently I was giving unsolicited instructions.
I don't need applause for doing the right thing. A small acknowledgment would be appropriate.
My character defects are very concerned about these proposed changes.
I woke up willing. Then I checked my messages.
I can let things go. I just like to give them a lengthy farewell speech.
I used to avoid my problems. Now I discuss them over coffee while avoiding them.
My sponsor suggested action. I was really enjoying the research phase.
I don't have to attend every argument I'm invited to. But the refreshments look promising.
I stopped trying to read minds. Now I'm working on not writing the dialogue for them.
I'm practicing being present. My brain stepped out to review an incident from 2009.
I asked for patience. I was expecting delivery, not homework.
Some of my best recovery work happens after I say, "Well, that's stupid."
I thought I had no expectations. Then someone failed to meet one.
My ego has agreed to step aside. It would like a farewell party.
I can admit when I'm wrong. It helps if nobody is around when it happens.
I planned a peaceful morning. My coffee maker had a different understanding of the program.
I don't need to control the meeting. I just have thoughts about the chairs, the topic, and how we're doing this.
I took the cotton out of my ears. My mouth has requested legal representation.
My sponsor said to sleep on it. I stayed up thinking about whether that was good advice.
I'm giving people the benefit of the doubt. Some are using their entire allowance before breakfast.
Recovery taught me to tell on myself. I was much better at telling on everyone else.
I finally admitted I couldn't run the universe. I was hoping to retain a regional position.
I know feelings aren't facts. Mine have prepared a very convincing presentation.
I'm practicing restraint of tongue and pen. Nobody mentioned the group chat.
I was ready for a spiritual experience. They asked me to take out the trash.
I didn't make a mountain out of a molehill today. I did request a survey.
I let someone finish their sentence. I would like that entered into the minutes.
My meditation went well. I solved three imaginary arguments and remembered we need dish soap.
I can laugh at myself now. Occasionally after a brief investigation into who else is laughing.
My sponsor asked if I'd prayed about it. I had mostly been providing God with updates on the other person's behavior.
I want to be useful. Preferably at a time that works for me and without stacking chairs.
I have stopped keeping score. I'm just aware of the current standings.
The newcomer asked when it gets easier. Three people laughed, which wasn't the brochure I would've chosen.
I'm letting go of perfection. I'd like to do it correctly.
I thought "easy does it" meant somebody else would do it.
I have a daily reprieve. My attitude would prefer a lifetime exemption.
Today I kept my side of the street clean. I did look across the road several times.
I said, "I could be wrong." My voice made it clear this was a theoretical possibility.
I believe in a power greater than myself. The self-checkout machine remains a difficult relationship.
My apology was going beautifully until I added "but."
I made a decision to turn my will over. My will asked whether we could discuss it after lunch.
I didn't send the angry text. It remains available as a draft for historical purposes.
I thought I was being honest. Turns out honesty doesn't require a closing argument.
I can stay sober through anything. Apparently "anything" includes the printer not connecting.
I asked my sponsor for a second opinion. He repeated the first one more slowly.
I'm getting comfortable with silence. The person beside me might be mad, though. We should probably check.
My morning prayer was sincere. My afternoon behavior is still catching up.
I don't need everyone to like me. I would appreciate a list of the exceptions and their reasons.
I thought taking inventory meant counting how many times I'd been misunderstood.
I made coffee for the meeting. Suddenly everybody had a fourth tradition about how strong it should be.
I left my comfort zone. It called twice to ask when I'd be home.
I'm learning that "no" is a complete sentence. Mine usually comes with a documentary.
I don't chase chaos anymore. Sometimes I do peek through the blinds.
I started the day with a clean slate. My brain restored a backup.
I'm taking suggestions. Implementation remains under review.
I thought I'd reached emotional maturity. Then somebody used my mug.
I'm not avoiding the conversation. I'm waiting for the perfect combination of courage and them bringing it up.
My sponsor told me to call before I do something stupid. We are negotiating what counts as "before."
I got to the meeting early to help. Accidentally found myself in a conversation about how nobody helps.
I asked for clarity. The answer was "you should apologize," so I asked again.
I am powerless over other people. Their choice of speakerphone volume makes this especially clear.
I'm practicing gratitude for what I have. The delivery app thinks I could still have fries.
I stopped expecting people to read my mind. Now I sigh at a volume they should understand.
I have learned to accept uncertainty. I'd like to know how long we'll be doing that.
My phone tells me my screen time is up. I don't remember asking it to take my inventory.
I'm learning to rest without guilt. So far I'm lying down and worrying in a different position.
I asked whether there was an easier way. Nobody even checked the supply closet.
I stayed out of somebody else's business today. It looked poorly supervised.
I thought serenity would make me mysterious and wise. Mostly it stops me from replying immediately.
I took responsibility for my actions. My intentions would still like to testify.
My sponsor said, "Have you eaten?" I had prepared a much more complicated explanation for my mood.
I used to wake up wondering what happened. Now I wake up remembering, and sometimes that's its own inconvenience.
I am willing to change. I would prefer the changes to involve other people appreciating me more.
I stopped saying yes to everything. My calendar is relieved. My guilt has opened an investigation.
Today I gave someone space. I did wonder what they were doing with it.
I went for a walk to clear my head. My thoughts insisted on coming along.
I said I was fine. My sponsor asked the kind of follow-up question that ruins a perfectly good performance.
I didn't interrupt the speaker. I completed their story privately at twice the speed.
I'm supposed to identify, not compare. Unfortunately, comparing was one of my stronger qualifications.
I learned that boredom won't kill me. It does submit frequent complaints.
I brought my problem to a meeting. Somebody else had already used it for the topic.
I cleaned up a mess without mentioning who made it. Please appreciate how difficult it was to write only that sentence.
My higher power and I have a good relationship. I explain the situation. Then I explain it again in case the first version didn't convey the urgency.
I'm learning to enjoy the journey. I would still like access to the estimated arrival time.
I said, "Whatever you think is best." Then discovered they had an actual opinion.
I don't expect recovery to fix everything. But I did think I'd lose my keys less.
I got honest about my fear. It was wearing a very convincing outfit called "being realistic."
I can handle criticism. I just need several hours to explain why it's inaccurate.
I went to a different meeting for a different answer. Apparently the groups have been talking.
I practiced patience in traffic. The lesson continued all the way through the grocery store.
I stopped making everything about me. Then wondered whether everyone had noticed.
Today I helped without expecting anything back. Tomorrow's attitude has not yet signed the agreement.
I used to hide my drinking. Now I hide from the person asking for volunteers.
I thought the fourth step would explain why I was upset. It included several reasons other people might be upset with me.
I had a moment of serenity. Naturally, I tried to figure out how to reproduce it permanently.
I said what I meant without saying it mean. My vocabulary had to make some last-minute adjustments.
I'm working on being less defensive. What exactly are you implying by that?
I asked God to guide my feet. They went to a meeting instead of where I had planned, which felt a little personal.
I can enjoy my own company now. We still disagree about bedtime.
I thought I'd let that resentment go. Apparently I had only minimized the window.
I told my sponsor the short version. He asked whether there was, in fact, a short version.
I don't need to explain myself to everybody. This is unfortunate because I'd already rehearsed it in the shower.
I'm staying in my lane. I have observations about several adjacent lanes.
I put principles before personalities. Some personalities require me to reread the instructions.
My recovery plan was going great until it required me to do my recovery plan.
I went to bed with a clear conscience. My brain brought up an awkward goodbye from six years ago anyway.
I handled rejection gracefully. My imaginary acceptance speech will need a new venue.
I discovered I can survive being misunderstood. I have not yet stopped drafting the explanation.
I took a suggestion that wasn't my idea. Please respect my privacy during this difficult time.
I made amends without asking to be forgiven. My ego waited in the car with the engine running.
I thought "more will be revealed" meant I'd get everybody else's secrets.
I reached out instead of isolating. Someone answered, which meant I had to go through with it.
I am grateful to remember the whole evening. Especially the part where I said goodbye and stayed another forty minutes.
I let a good day be a good day. Only checked for hidden problems twice.
My sponsor suggested a meeting. I had been hoping for something I could order online.
I don't need to win every conversation. Some of these people are taking full advantage.
I asked for a peaceful life. Turns out I'm expected to stop participating in the optional nonsense.
Another day sober. Still weird, but now I can account for most of it.
